gap: The value of peripheral (non-answer-chain) context triples has been tested only at inference time, where they are nearly inert (+0.003 F1) and inflated context adds accuracy-depressing distractors. No retrieved study tests whether peripheral context triples contribute to the learned representation during training, or whether they are simply noise that also harms training.

evidence.quote: Holding the number of triples fixed and replacing every triple that is not on the chain with material from an unrelated entity changes answer accuracy by +0.003 F1, while removing the chain costs most of what the graph was worth.

why_unaddressed: The closest controlled evidence is an inference-time prompt-composition study over gold subgraphs, and the training-time works found supervise paths, embeddings, or executable queries without a peripheral-context arm at matched budget. So the question is untested on the training side.
research_question: Do peripheral same-passage context triples improve multi-hop KGQA when they appear in training supervision, or is any observed gain explained by the reasoning chain and/or token budget alone?
potential_experiment: Train three arms at matched token budget and identical templates: isolated triples/paths; chain + same-passage peripheral triples; chain + shuffled/unrelated triples of equal length. Evaluate each under identical inference context and report per-hop Hits@1 and one-hop failure rate; the shuffled arm isolates whether any gain is due to relevance versus added tokens.
verification_required: Search for training-time ablations of context relevance in graph-augmented fine-tuning (random vs relevant subgraph at matched budget) and for work on distractor robustness in KG-grounded language model training; confirm no such matched-budget training ablation already exists.
